newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean students surrender after killing.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean students surrender after killing.

text.p: South Korea's militant pro-Pyongyang campus body on Thursday handed over to authorities four students it said witnessed the fatal beating of a man suspected of being a police informer, a police official said.
The four members of the outlawed Hanchongryon -- two men and two women -- surrendered at a police post.
"The Hanchongryon turned over four students who they claim were witnesses to the incident," the police official said.
Earlier, Hanchongryon chairman Kang Eui-won expressed deep regret over the death and apologised. In a statement, he vowed to turn over witnesses to the beating and those actually responsible.
The group had already admitted responsibility for the violent death of the man, whose badly bruised body was delivered to a hospital in Hanyang University on Wednesday.
He had been beaten and his wrists roped together during an lengthy interrogation in the student union building to extract a confession that he was a spy, according to a Hanchongryon account.
A police official said autopsy reports on Thursday showed the victim, identified by the police as Lee Suk, a 22-year-old worker, died as a direct result of the battering.

"His body was covered with bruises which seem to have come from baton blows, punches and kicks, and there are rope marks on his wrists which suggest he was tied," the official said. The victim had lost a large amount of blood.
Prime Minister Koh Kun vowed to put an end to campus violence and ordered the arrest of Hanchongryon leaders by the end of June.
"I'm sorry to the public that this enormous disruption in the capital was not prevented," Koh was quoted as saying in a statement.

Students demanding the resignation of President Kim Young-sam and details of his 1992 election spending went on the rampage last Friday. Since then there have been frequent clashes between tear-gas firing police and militant students wielding metal pipes and hurling firebombs.
A riot policeman died during clashes around Hanyang University on Monday. His funeral was held on Thursday.
In his statement, Hanchongryon chairman Kang said his group would "cooperate with legal procedures and turn over those involved and those who witnessed the incident".
"We deeply regret our actions and apologise to the Korean people," Kang said.
But he added: "Hanchongryon will continue to demand the resignation of Kim Young-sam and the revelation of details of Kim Young-sam's election funding."
Opposition parties allege the president massively overspent to get elected, and are demanding a full accounting.

On Thursday, Hanchongryon students held an inauguration ceremony at Seoul National University for new office holders. They also laid flowers at a small shrine on the campus in honour of the two men who died.

Later, a new flare-up occurred when students seized six policemen outside the campus and held them for about 20 minutes, a police official said. The officers were released, but students kept their walkie-talkie handsets.
In an earlier crackdown on the Hanchongryon last August, 151 of its leaders were rounded up and jailed.
